newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey H1 '96 C/A deficit estimate $4 bln - Minister.
newsitem.headline: Turkey H1 '96 C/A deficit estimate $4 bln - Minister.

text.p: Turkish State Minister Ufuk Soylemez said on Thursday provisional figures showed the current account was expected to show a deficit of $4 billion in first-half 1996.

"According to estimates, exports stood at $10.9 billion, imports at $21.3 billion in the first six months of 1996 and the trade balance showed a $10.4 billion deficit," Soylemez told parliament's budgetary commission.
"However, strong tourism income and invisible credits caused the current account balance to end with a provisional $4 billion deficit in the same six-month period," he said.
Soylemez added that the introduction of a six percent levy on some imports in July 1996 was expected to slow down the rapid increase in imports in the second half of 1996.
Release of Turkey's official trade data has been delayed by technical difficulties arising from the customs union with the European Union which took effect in January.

Turkish exports rose 15.7 percent to $5.50 billion in January-March from the same 1995 period, imports leapt 37.9 percent to $9.45 billion and the trade deficit surged 88.4 percent to $3.95 billion in the first three months, according to the State Institute of Statistics.
